content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Fort Collins

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your PMI Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a secondary degree plus defined project-management experience, or a high school diploma with substantially more experience. Review PMI's education and hours-worked thresholds now to confirm you qualify, then gather documentation of your project roles and responsibilities for your application.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp instructor-led course. Attend synchronous sessions from your Fort Collins location on a schedule that fits your work and life. Our active certified practitioners deliver real-world context and exam-focused instruction across all five process groups.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing your 35 contact hours, file your PMP application directly with PMI. Include proof of your education, work experience, and course completion. Pay PMI's exam fee and await application approval before you can schedule your exam appointment.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and review sessions—to solidify your knowledge. Schedule your proctored exam online and take it from a quiet location in or near Fort Collins. Plan for a rigorous, scenario-based assessment of your project-management competency.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: Earn professional development units (PDUs) over each three-year renewal cycle through training, volunteer work, and professional activities. Renew your credential with PMI before it expires. Staying current keeps your PMP active and demonstrates ongoing commitment to the profession.
